subject: Post-call: hybrid deployment qualification + cost sketch
summary: Post-demo qualification thread to clarify deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and share initial cost back-of-envelope. Agreed next step: Redwood to send 3 scenario cost sketches and draft MAP; customer to confirm data residency and expected peak TPS.
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@horizonai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: hybrid deployment qualification + cost sketch

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to hear more about HorizonAI's production plan and SLAs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- What we heard from you:
  * Primary requirement: low-latency <200ms p95 for interactive assistant traffic (peak 600 TPS burstable to 1k)
  * Data sensitivity: training data is internal PII-minimized but audit logs must remain in your VPC for 7 years
  * Preference to avoid per-token surprises for high-volume inference — finance prefers capex-like predictability if we can match unit economics

- Redwood qualification thoughts (high-level):
  * Hosted API: fastest to prod, good for initial rollout. Per-token billing — strong if average token size and request distribution are stable. Potentially risky on costs at scale without reserved burst or token caps.
  * Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, better cost control for sustained high TPS (we can build reservation bands). Requires commit (monthly/annual) but we can structure burst and overage terms.
  * Private VPC / on-prem: necessary for the audit log residency requirement; higher ops overhead and licensing, but allows you to own logs and KMS. Could be hybrid: Dedicated in Redwood-managed infra for public traffic + Private VPC for sensitive audit writes.

Attached: a short back-of-envelope PDF with three scenarios (hosted per-token baseline, dedicated 3-node reserve, private VPC baseline) and a draft MAP for timelines.

Can you confirm the following so we can finalize the numbers: 1) expected average tokens per request (or a sample distribution), 2) % of traffic that must route to on-prem/VPC (if any), and 3) committed term Horizon would consider for reserved capacity (monthly vs annual)?

Proposed next step: we will produce a formal 3-scenario pricing sketch and a one-page MAP by EOD Tuesday. If that works, we'll loop in your procurement contact and schedule a short sync to walk the numbers.

Thanks —
Rachel

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mailto:rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Horizon_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx (xlsx), Redwood-cost-scenarios-back-of-envelope.pdf (pdf)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@horizonai.com>

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: hybrid deployment qualification + cost sketch

Rachel — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Average tokens per request is around 180 tokens; however, 20% of calls are long-form (700–1,200 tokens) during nightly bulk summarization. Interactive assistant traffic is the bursty part (180 tokens).
2) Initially ~10% of traffic needs to have audit log writes to our VPC (we need those logs off-platform); that fraction may grow to 30% for regulated cohorts.
3) Procurement preference: start with a 6–12 month committed band for dedicated capacity if the math works; otherwise monthly is tolerable for a pilot.

Also — can you give an initial sense for the break-even point where dedicated reserved capacity becomes cheaper than hosted per-token? Rough rule of thumb is fine for now.

Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, HorizonAI

Liam / Rachel — putting a quick back-of-envelope here so we can answer the break-even question. Assumptions flagged inline.

Short summary (rule of thumb): if sustained interactive traffic averages >450–550 TPS equivalent (with moderate token length) you generally see Dedicated cost advantage vs Hosted per-token for inference costs alone. Key caveat: Hosted includes operational overhead and near-zero ops burden to Horizon; Dedicated requires commit but better unit pricing.

BOE numbers (very simplified):
- Hosted per-token: $0.000022 per input+output token (example blended rate)
  * Avg tokens/request (interactive): 180 -> cost/request = 180 * 0.000022 = $0.00396 (~$0.004)
  * At 600 TPS sustained -> $0.004 * 600 * 3600 * 24 = ~$207,360 per day (note bursts are higher)

- Dedicated reserved (example 3x A100-equivalent pool): monthly commit $50k/month for baseline pool (includes infra + support); that pool handles ~X tokens/sec (we'll size properly once you share distribution).
  * If your sustained daily spend on hosted > $50k/month equivalent then dedicated is likely cheaper.

- Private VPC: +20–40% on top of Dedicated due to egress, management, and licensing; also one-time onboarding.

Given your numbers (avg 180 tokens with 600 TPS burst target and 10% on-VPC), my quick callout: run the hosted math on your monthly volume; if expected monthly hosted spend crosses ~$35–60k/month, start formal dedicated sizing/commit conversation.

I'll take horizon's token distribution (if you can share a sample) and produce a formal three-scenario spreadsheet with line-item assumptions by Tuesday EOD.

Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
